summary: Al Thaurah Airport (SOR) is a small airfield located in eastern Syria near the Euphrates River valley, serving the town of Al-Thawrah in the Deir ez-Zor Governorate. The facility primarily supports limited general aviation and occasional regional flights rather than scheduled commercial service. Its remote desert-adjacent location places it close to some of Syria's most significant archaeological sites, including the ancient ruins of Dura-Europos.
faqs:
Q: Does Al Thaurah Airport have scheduled commercial flights?
A: No, SOR is a small airfield with no regular scheduled commercial service. Operations are typically limited to private, charter, or military flights.

Q: Where is Al Thaurah Airport located relative to major Syrian cities?
A: It is situated in eastern Syria, roughly 100 km southeast of Deir ez-Zor and well over 300 km northeast of Damascus, in a relatively remote area near the Euphrates River.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: As a small airport, SOR offers basic infrastructure with limited passenger amenities. Travelers should not expect large terminals, extensive retail, or comprehensive ground services.

Q: Is the airport accessible to foreign travelers?
A: Access to this region of Syria is restricted due to ongoing security concerns. Travelers should consult their government travel advisories and check current conditions before considering any visit.
transport_tips: Ground transport options at Al Thaurah Airport are very limited, so arranging private transportation in advance is strongly recommended. The nearest major road connections are along routes linking Deir ez-Zor to other parts of eastern Syria. Travelers should expect long road journeys to reach any major city or border crossing.
local_tip: If visiting the region for archaeological purposes, note that the ancient site of Dura-Europos—one of the world's oldest known Christian house churches—is located relatively nearby and can be combined with a trip through this area for those with appropriate security clearance and local guidance.
